brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.evidence: Three full-depth bins bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,0,0 and bin:1,0,0 (hex-bin-full), one in each of the three cells in a row.

Three hex-acc-keyhole keyhole hanger accessories (accessory:0#-1,0#2, accessory:0#0,0#2, accessory:0#1,0#2), one on the rear face (slot 2) of each cell, so the rack lifts onto wall screws. Slots on the seam faces between cells were refused (SEAM_FLAT), so all hangers sit on the shared outside rear face.

Three open-top full-depth bins in a row for spice pots; staged with a tumbler in each bin to show stored jars. Note: load capacity and material suitability are not checked by the configurator; the parts are printed in a user-chosen material.

finish.summary: A 3-cell row spice rack: three full-depth bins side by side, each cell carrying a keyhole hanger on the rear face so the whole rack lifts onto wall screws. Open faces capped and joints locked; tumblers staged in the bins to show spice storage. check_build passes with meshClash clear.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
